source.quote: So, one of the main unlocks of Dun Morogh was getting access to a new crafting alt, Golden Path. This frees up the alt to learn two professions forever and never unlearn them, and Goldie can feed him crafting materials to craft with them. Now, the ones we ended up choosing were leatherworking and blacksmithing, for good reason. Because last mailbox opening, I noticed that we actually sold out of the Loch Modan Bearskin Rugs, the leatherworking decor craft. Those things not only look super clean, but they also sell. So, our first order of business on Goldie this week is to farm up enough to restock the supply and get it over to Golden Path, our crafting alt, to make a few. So, the farm list, we need 120 rugged leather and 20 cured rugged hides. Luckily, rugged hides drop from the same mobs who skin down into rugged leather. And the best place to do that off the Sunken Temple for a few trash runs for skinning. Because once we get our skinning high enough, they start dropping rugged leather and rugged hide, which we need. We have a lot of progress to make here, but first, let me tell you about the sponsor of today's episode.

source.quote: While it would be the most efficient, we wouldn't discover the gems in Dun Morogh, which is the real journey. But that being said, we can go back to these zones to restock in the materials we unlocked with them, which is why we find ourselves in the Sunken Temple getting rugged leather or Molten Core to restock dark iron every now and then. I like to think of the old zones more of our shopping center for crafts, but not the day-in-day-out office. Oh, wait. What? Stealthblade. Stealthblade just dropped. This is something wild. We were farming here for hours in Sunken Temple for one of the ultra-rare blue items during our Swamp of Sorrows unlock, and this, it was one of the big ones. At over 500,000 market value, a decent sale rate, and a region average sale price over 250,000 gold. This has to be the best drop we've gotten in the series so far. The second closest might have been the Blackvenom Blade from Row the Silent in Redridge, but this, if we can sell it even anywhere close to the average sale price, is basically a full wild token.

We're over halfway, and we just got some massive progress. Getting back into Dun Morogh, last episode we scoured Coldridge Valley and Tinkertown for some of the rare white drops that have solid market value for transmog and maybe more so for collectors, but I think it's time to clean up the rest of Dun Morogh because there are actually a few more drops like this hiding around. source.quote: The Frostmane Snowstriders have a small axe, the Frostmane Axe, which has a low drop rate, reported below 1% and a market value anywhere from 15,000 gold to 37,000 gold. Although, region sale averages on this item are closer to just over 1,000 gold, but hey, even if we can get a sale at 1,000 gold, that's 1,000 gold in the pockets. And I will definitely put a few on the auction house. We only need to farm and sell 230 to get the next zone, right? Then, the Frostmane Seers, they also have a drop worth farming. Again, with a low drop rate, reported on Wowhead at 0.2%, but that is probably artificially lowered because these items were also unavailable for a few expansions. But the value on the Frostmane Staff isn't bad. It's about 10,000 gold market value, and the average sale clocks in around 500 gold, although the sale rate is pretty low. But if you're already farming the axe, we may as well take a few of the seers while we're here. I think they're on the same spot anyways, so it just increases rates on the axes as well. And leaving Shimmering Ridge, a little further to the east out in Dun Morogh, another beast to farm. Out in the Thandol Hills is the home to the Iceclaw Bear. And this must be a rough spot for bear attacks because the drop we're looking for is the Mountaineer's Chestpiece. A white rare drop again, like most in Dun Morogh, with an item value of around 6,000 gold and sales anywhere between there and 1,000 gold.

source.quote: So, definitely not a bad piece as far as expected value to collect and post on the auction house. And to round off the Dun Morogh transmog loop, out even further to the east in the Gol'Bolar Quarry are quite a few troggs, and well, they are also worth farming for a little while. So, first up are the Skull thumpers, who drop both the Skull Hatchet and the Trogg Club. Both of these are items with some decent market value. Then, there is the Rockjaw Bone Snapper. And these guys also worth tagging. They can drop the Frostbit Staff, which ironically is one of the ones we got on double down in classic WoW, but it is back in the game again as a white transmog item. And I wouldn't expect any crazy sales on these, but like I said, they're definitely good enough to keep stocked on the auction house shelves cuz one day, a random collector might come through and get one of each. Which, with the troggs accounted for, I do think that rounds out the white transmog here in Dun Morogh. And across all Tinkertown, Coldridge, and out in Dun Morogh here, there are quite a few items that actually have decent value. So, I have just gone around and gotten one to three copies of each for the auction house listings because with our current cash stack and the wild token target of 230,000 gold, even just a few of these selling per week, even below market value, can really help the numbers, especially since we haven't gotten any consistent farms that clock over 4,000 gold per hour here in Dun Morogh. But that might change because one seasonal event that's rolling into town now may very well increase our gold per hour in Dun Morogh. And that event is Noble Garden. So, across all Azeroth, mainly around the inns such as Goldshire, Kharanos, and around Brill, is a festive holiday event. Now, there are a few quests to be done, but this event is a little different than a lot of the other holiday events in World of Warcraft, and it's largely in Goldie's favor. So, a lot of holiday events require currency to be acquired over time and usually over the course of the event, either through doing dailies that often lead outside of starting zones, or through other mechanics that require visiting a bunch of other zones. But in Noble Garden, around the inns are a bunch of hidden, brightly colored eggs. And the one daily quest in town is to collect 20 of them, open them up, and hand in the shells. Now, this daily quest alone won't give us much gold on Goldie, but a daily dose of 12,000 experience is definitely no small amount and should give us about a half a bar of XP per day. Not bad and better than the 50 XP per node we're currently getting, but when opening up the egg, most of the time they contain one Noble Garden Chocolate, a food, but also the currency for the event. And the bonus for us, even though the quest is for 20, there is no cap to how many eggs you can hunt for and open up around these towns. And well, we have both Dun Morogh's Kharanos and Elwynn Forest's Goldshire unlocked, so the hunt begins. But inside the egg, aside from chocolate, you can also get a few festive items for appearances or even some low value pets, but the big ticket item is a mount, a BOE mount, meaning it can be sold on the auction house. Now, I couldn't find the actual drop rates of the mount from the egg anywhere, but it's likely between 1 and 1,000 to 1 and 2,000. And the mount in question is the Swift Spring Strider, which goes for a hefty 30,000 to 40,000 gold on the auction house. Not a bad ticket price. Of course, as the event goes on, the supply in the market may very well go up and the price may trickle down a little bit with it. So, do we just farm eggs until we get lucky and pull the mount from one of them?

source.quote: But to make the runs just a little bit more efficient, both from a gold perspective, but also from a time perspective, I have been swapping to enchanting whenever I do my runs. There's quite a few greens that are below my auction house listing price. I only list items on my auction house tune that are about 700 gold or higher. source.quote: Uh yeah, still 26 or 27 runs through and no left binding but maybe soon. And at this point I am kind of rooting for either Deadwind Pass or Barrens on the zone spin but depending on if we get this next token today, we may not have to wait long to find out. But we have had a lot of excitement today with big drops and new events that bring crazy amount of gold but honestly, that is all super recent. And the reality of Dun Morogh, especially before Noble Garden, a lot of herb loops. I'm still doing the same laps around the zone taking out the rare spawns for a chance at some more loot, getting Silverleaf, Peacebloom and Earthroot then swapping to inscription to mill the herbs into pigments and either sell the Alabaster pigments or convert them into Moon Glow inks. The standard Dun Morogh shuffle. And in the past week or so, I have really haven't found a better consistent gold farm here in Dun Morogh for Goldy. Of course, with the Darkmoon Faire in town which it currently is, I am trying to keep my head on and every hour on the hour use the on use to get a free Darkmoon Pool in Dun Morogh or wherever I am which adds about 250 to 500 gold per hour pretty passively. As well, for a little while there during a quick restock of frayed knots, I thought that Blizzard had actually nerfed the drop rates from the airstrip. After some further testing with a decent sample size, it turns out just like any other drop, it is variable and I have since had quite a few good sessions there that reached about the same knots per hour as the first session or even better. So, it But while we're doing these Dun Morogh farms crafting some day cooler on the crafting alts and farming around, I do think Dun Morogh is likely to hit the second highest slash played of gold bound so far second only of course to Elwynn Forest but maybe that would have been different if I had started Elwynn during Noble Garden. But speaking of Noble Garden, well, we aren't actually done farming chocolates for gold. It's actually crazy here because there are two more things from the vendor worth getting, a couple of pets. First up is the Noble Garden Bunny. Now, the market value on this guy is pretty high and it's pretty often you'll see a very high listing price but the average sale price for this guy is also decent around 10,000 gold but because it has been available for so long, the sale rate is quite low probably because a lot of accounts already have this. But for 200 chocolate and a potential 10,000 gold sale at some point, I do think it's worth grabbing. Then there is the Lovely Duckling and I mean, just look at it. Who wouldn't want this little guy? And at first glance, it kind of looks like it's soulbound and that it couldn't be sold because there's no auction house data that shows up and that's probably what a lot of people think. But this guy, like Don Anthias' cats, can actually be learned and then placed in a cage to be sold and he sells a lot more frequently with an average sale price around 15,000 gold once caged which gives a pretty on par gold per egg as the mount itself. So, we officially have three targets and travelers, this egg farming is so fun and so high in theoretical gold per hour that I farmed up a couple of each popping between Dun Morogh and Elwynn doing my dailies, killing the rare every day. So, the transmog alt is stocked to the brim with Noble Garden supplies and I am just hoping for some sales. And for Goldy, I am a really trying to get out of Dun Morogh today so I'm going to list these at competitive prices but if you want to try farming these yourselves, it really might be best to get a couple copies of each and hold onto them for a few months for the markets to recover because the longer away from the event that you sell them, generally the higher price you'll get. But with all that said, I think it's time to get in there and take a look at the auction house. And before we open the mailbox, a quick reminder to check out Raid through the link in the description to access the free legendary champions. We're currently sitting at 117,000 gold and the WoW token is at 231k so we are over halfway, and just barely.
